1	//! Evaluation error types.
2	
3	use mlpl_core::LabeledShape;
4	
5	/// Errors produced during evaluation.
6	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
7	pub enum EvalError {
8	    /// No expressions to evaluate.
9	    EmptyInput,
10	    /// Variable not found in environment.
11	    UndefinedVariable(String),
12	    /// Feature not yet implemented.
13	    Unsupported(String),
14	    /// Error from array operations.
15	    ArrayError(mlpl_array::ArrayError),
16	    /// Repeat count must be a scalar.
17	    InvalidRepeatCount,
18	    /// Tensor constructor shape dimension must be a non-negative scalar integer.
19	    InvalidShapeDim,
20	    /// Error from built-in function dispatch.
21	    RuntimeError(mlpl_runtime::RuntimeError),
22	    /// Expected an array value but got a string.
23	    ExpectedArray,
24	    /// Expected a string value but got something else.
25	    ExpectedString,
26	    /// Saga R1 step 002: a CPU op tried to consume a
27	    /// `Value::DeviceTensor` whose bytes live on a
28	    /// peer server. Strict-fault: the user must
29	    /// explicitly `to_device('cpu', x)` to fetch.
30	    DeviceTensorFault {
31	        /// Peer URL the tensor lives on.
32	        peer: String,
33	        /// Device name on that peer (e.g., `"mlx"`).
34	        device: String,
35	    },
36	    /// Wrong number of arguments to a built-in.
37	    BadArity {
38	        /// Function name.
39	        func: String,
40	        /// Expected count.
41	        expected: usize,
42	        /// Got count.
43	        got: usize,
44	    },
45	    /// Error from the visualization layer.
46	    VizError(mlpl_viz::VizError),
47	    /// Two operand shapes (or labels) disagree in a way the named op
48	    /// cannot resolve. Saga 11.5 Phase 4: replaces string
49	    /// `Unsupported` messages for broadcasting and contraction
50	    /// failures. `expected` and `actual` are the left- and right-hand
51	    /// operand labeled shapes respectively.
52	    ShapeMismatch {
53	        /// Operator or builtin name (`"add"`, `"matmul"`, ...).
54	        op: String,
55	        /// Left-hand operand's labeled shape.
56	        expected: LabeledShape,
57	        /// Right-hand operand's labeled shape.
58	        actual: LabeledShape,
59	    },
60	    /// Two tensors (or a tensor and the active `device("...") { }`
61	    /// scope) disagree on device placement. Saga 14 step 005: raised
62	    /// by `apply(model, X)` when the input lives on a different
63	    /// device than the model's parameters, and by any op that
64	    /// receives mixed-device operands. `op` names the site
65	    /// (`"matmul"`, `"apply"`, `"add"`, ...); `expected` is the
66	    /// device the left-hand side carries and `actual` is the
67	    /// right-hand side's.
68	    DeviceMismatch {
69	        /// Operator or builtin name.
70	        op: String,
71	        /// Device the left-hand (or first) operand is on.
72	        expected: String,
73	        /// Device the right-hand (or second) operand is on.
74	        actual: String,
75	    },
76	    /// Saga 23 step 004: a typed-value consumer received an
77	    /// argument whose `ValueTag` does not satisfy the
78	    /// predicate. `expected` is the tag-display-name the
79	    /// consumer wants ("Logit", "Loss", ...), `actual` is the
80	    /// tag-display-name the argument carries, and `hint` is a
81	    /// 3-5 line tutoring message naming the most likely cause
82	    /// and one or two concrete fixes. Untagged arguments
83	    /// always pass and never raise this error (gradual-typing
84	    /// additivity).
85	    TypeMismatch {
86	        /// Consumer op name.
87	        op: String,
88	        /// Tag the consumer wants.
89	        expected: String,
90	        /// Tag the argument actually carries.
91	        actual: String,
92	        /// Tutoring hint (multi-line ASCII text).
93	        hint: String,
94	    },
95	    /// Saga 21.5 step 003: cooperative cancellation observed at a
96	    /// loop head or pre-builtin checkpoint. `step` is the
97	    /// inner-most loop iteration the eval was on when the trip was
98	    /// caught (`0` for non-loop sites). `partial_losses` is the
99	    /// per-iteration loss curve accumulated so far inside `train`
100	    /// (empty for `for` / `repeat` / pre-builtin sites). The
101	    /// session's `last_losses` binding is also populated with the
102	    /// same vector so post-cancel `:vars` still sees the partial
103	    /// curve.
104	    Cancelled {
105	        /// Iteration index at the trip site (0 for non-loop).
106	        step: usize,
107	        /// Per-iteration losses recorded so far inside `train`.
108	        partial_losses: Vec<f64>,
109	    },
110	}
111	
112	impl std::fmt::Display for EvalError {
113	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
114	        match self {
115	            Self::EmptyInput => write!(f, "empty input"),
116	            Self::UndefinedVariable(name) => write!(f, "undefined variable: {name}"),
117	            Self::InvalidRepeatCount => write!(f, "repeat count must be a scalar integer"),
118	            Self::InvalidShapeDim => {
119	                write!(f, "shape dimension must be a non-negative scalar integer")
120	            }
121	            Self::Unsupported(msg) => write!(f, "unsupported: {msg}"),
122	            Self::ArrayError(e) => write!(f, "array error: {e}"),
123	            Self::RuntimeError(e) => write!(f, "{e}"),
124	            Self::ExpectedArray => write!(f, "expected an array value, got a string"),
125	            Self::ExpectedString => write!(f, "expected a string value"),
126	            Self::DeviceTensorFault { peer, device } => write!(
127	                f,
128	                "tensor lives on {peer}:{device}; \
129	                 use to_device('cpu', x) to fetch"
130	            ),
131	            Self::BadArity {
132	                func,
133	                expected,
134	                got,
135	            } => {
136	                write!(f, "{func} expects {expected} arguments, got {got}")
137	            }
138	            Self::VizError(e) => write!(f, "{e}"),
139	            Self::ShapeMismatch {
140	                op,
141	                expected,
142	                actual,
143	            } => write!(f, "{op}: expected {expected}, got {actual}"),
144	            Self::DeviceMismatch {
145	                op,
146	                expected,
147	                actual,
148	            } => write!(f, "device mismatch: {op} on {expected} vs {actual}"),
149	            Self::TypeMismatch {
150	                op,
151	                expected,
152	                actual,
153	                hint,
154	            } => write!(
155	                f,
156	                "type mismatch in {op}: expected {expected}, got {actual}\n  hint: {hint}"
157	            ),
158	            Self::Cancelled {
159	                step,
160	                partial_losses,
161	            } => write!(
162	                f,
163	                "cancelled at step {step} ({} losses)",
164	                partial_losses.len()
165	            ),
166	        }
167	    }
168	}
169	
170	impl std::error::Error for EvalError {}
171	
172	impl From<mlpl_array::ArrayError> for EvalError {
173	    fn from(e: mlpl_array::ArrayError) -> Self {
174	        Self::ArrayError(e)
175	    }
176	}
177	
178	impl From<mlpl_runtime::RuntimeError> for EvalError {
179	    fn from(e: mlpl_runtime::RuntimeError) -> Self {
180	        Self::RuntimeError(e)
181	    }
182	}
183	
184	impl From<mlpl_viz::VizError> for EvalError {
185	    fn from(e: mlpl_viz::VizError) -> Self {
186	        Self::VizError(e)
187	    }
188	}

input.new_string:
### `POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/cancel`

Cooperatively cancel an in-flight eval on the session.
Added in Saga 21.5 step 003. **Authenticated** (bearer
token, same as `/eval`). Idempotent: a second `POST
/cancel` after the bool is already set is a no-op.

Request:

```http
POST /v1/sessions/<id>/cancel
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

{}
```

Body is ignored (use `{}` or omit entirely).

Response (`200 OK`) on success:

```json
{"cancelled": true}
```

Error responses match `/eval`:

- **`401 Unauthorized`** -- missing or wrong bearer.
- **`404 Not Found`** -- unknown `session_id`.

Mechanism:

- Every session has a `tokio` interrupt token kept in
  a parallel `InterruptMap` alongside the session
  record. `/cancel` reads that map (NOT the sessions
  map) so it can fire while an in-flight `/eval` or
  `/eval_stream` holds the sessions write lock or has
  removed the session for the duration of the call.
- The bearer-token check uses the copy of the token
  stored in the `InterruptMap` entry, for the same
  reason.
- Flipping the bool trips the in-flight eval at its
  next loop head (`for`, `train`, `repeat`) or
  pre-builtin checkpoint. The evaluator raises
  `EvalError::Cancelled { step, partial_losses }`;
  the SSE handler emits a terminal `event: cancelled`
  carrying both fields, and the non-streaming `/eval`
  handler returns a `400` with the Display formatting.
- Builtins do NOT yield mid-call. The cancellation
  latency floor is therefore "one op": a long-running
  `matmul` or `reduce_add` over a giant array finishes
  before the next pre-builtin check observes the
  cancel. A future saga can revisit if this bites in
  practice.
- After a cancel lands, the session is re-bindable
  for further evals. The eval handlers `reset()` the
  bool at the start of every call, so a prior cancel
  does not contaminate the next program.

SSE `event: cancelled` frame schema (Saga 21.5 step
003, in addition to the `ready` / `metric` / `done` /
`error` frames documented above):

```text
event: cancelled
data: {"step": 17, "partial_losses": [0.5, 1.5, ...]}
```

`step` is the iteration index the cancel landed on
(0 for non-loop sites); `partial_losses` is the
per-iteration loss curve accumulated by `train { ... }`
so far (empty for `for` / `repeat` / pre-builtin
sites). The session's `last_losses` binding is also
populated with the same vector, so post-cancel
`:vars` still surfaces the partial curve.

### `GET /v1/health`

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
saga 21.5 step 003: cooperative cancellation (/cancel + Interrupt + Ctrl-Ctrl-C)

Adds a session-scoped cancellation token that flips from the new
`POST /v1/sessions/<id>/cancel` endpoint and trips the in-flight
evaluator at the next loop head (`for`, `train`, `repeat`) or
pre-builtin checkpoint. On trip, `eval_train` enriches the
bubbled error with the current iteration index and the partial
loss curve accumulated so far; the SSE handler emits a terminal
`event: cancelled { step, partial_losses }`; `mlpl-repl --connect`
binds a double-Ctrl-C (within 2s) to a cancel POST and prints the
partial losses back to the user.

Layer-by-layer implementation:

- `crates/mlpl-eval/src/interrupt.rs` -- new `Interrupt` token
  (`Arc<AtomicBool>` with `new` / `set` / `reset` / `is_set`)
  plus `enrich_train_cancel` helper that stores the partial
  loss curve on `last_losses` and wraps the iteration index +
  losses into `EvalError::Cancelled` for `eval_train`'s
  `Result` signature.
- `crates/mlpl-eval/src/error.rs` -- new
  `EvalError::Cancelled { step: usize, partial_losses: Vec<f64> }`
  variant + Display impl.
- `crates/mlpl-eval/src/env.rs` -- `interrupt: Option<Interrupt>`
  field on `Environment` with `set_interrupt` / `clear_interrupt`
  / `check_interrupt` methods (the last returns `Err(Cancelled)`
  on trip so call sites just do `env.check_interrupt()?;`). Also
  extracted `emit_metrics(&self, step)` from `eval_train` to
  keep that function under the sw-checklist 50-line budget.
- `crates/mlpl-eval/src/eval.rs` + `eval_ops.rs` + `eval_for.rs`
  -- interrupt check at every loop head (`eval_train`,
  `eval_repeat`, `eval_for`) and before every builtin dispatch
  (`eval_fncall`). `eval_train` additionally catches bubbled
  `Cancelled` errors from deep in the body and re-emits them
  with its own iteration index + accumulated losses via
  `enrich_train_cancel`.
- `crates/mlpl-eval/src/lib.rs` -- export new `Interrupt` type
  alongside `EvalError` and `MetricSink`.

Server (`crates/mlpl-serve`):

- `sessions.rs` -- new `InterruptMap` / `InterruptEntry`
  parallel to the `SessionMap`. Stores the (token, Interrupt)
  pair keyed by session id so `/cancel` can authenticate AND
  flip the bool WITHOUT taking the sessions write lock (which
  is held by an in-flight `/eval` or has had the session
  removed by `/eval_stream`).
- `server.rs` -- `AppState` grows an `interrupts: InterruptMap`
  field; `build_app_with_peers` initializes it; new
  `POST /v1/sessions/:id/cancel` route.
- `handlers.rs` -- new `cancel_handler` (auth + bool flip,
  idempotent at the server level). New shared
  `install_session_interrupt` helper clones the session's
  Interrupt from the map, resets it, and installs it into the
  env; called by both `eval_handler` and `eval_stream_handler`.
  `eval_handler` also calls `clear_interrupt` on exit so the
  next eval starts clean.
- `lib.rs` sse mod -- `SseEvent::Cancelled { step, partial_losses }`
  variant; `eval_stream_handler`'s terminal-event match maps
  `EvalError::Cancelled` to this new variant instead of
  `SseEvent::Error`. SSE wire frame is
  `event: cancelled\ndata: {"step": N, "partial_losses": [...]}`.

Client (`apps/mlpl-repl`):

- `connect.rs` -- `ClientError::Cancelled { step, partial_losses }`
  variant + Display impl.
- `connect_stream.rs` -- new `should_double_cancel` debounce
  predicate (pure fn over previous-press Instant + window) plus
  `post_cancel` HTTP helper. `eval_remote_stream`'s
  `handle_frame` adds a `cancelled` event case that maps to
  `Err(ClientError::Cancelled { ... })`. `parse_connect_args`
  internalized the env-var truthiness check to keep the module
  function count under the sw-checklist budget.
- `connect_repl.rs` -- `read_loop` installs a SIGINT handler
  (via the `ctrlc` crate) that turns a double-Ctrl-C inside
  the 2s window into a `post_cancel`. `eval_and_print` handles
  the new `ClientError::Cancelled` arm by calling new
  `render_cancellation` (prints "cancelled at step N" plus a
  5-entry preview of the partial loss curve; the full curve
  remains in `last_losses` for `:vars`).
- `Cargo.toml` -- add `ctrlc = "3"` for the SIGINT binding.

Tests:

- `crates/mlpl-eval/tests/interrupt_tests.rs` -- 9 tests
  covering: no-interrupt baseline; installed-but-not-tripped
  is a no-op; cancel before train raises at step 0; cancel
  mid-train returns the partial loss curve via a custom
  MetricSink that flips the bool from a callback; cancel in
  `repeat` / `for` loops; cancel at pre-builtin checkpoint;
  cross-thread `Interrupt::set`; `reset()` clears the bool.
- `crates/mlpl-serve/tests/cancel_tests.rs` -- 5 tests:
  cancel mid-train via SSE returns `event: cancelled` with
  partial losses; cancel mid-builtin-loop returns promptly;
  double-cancel is idempotent (two POSTs both return 200);
  cancel requires bearer token (401); unknown session is 404.
- `apps/mlpl-repl/tests/connect_cancel_tests.rs` -- 5 tests:
  first/second/timed-out Ctrl-C debounce predicate;
  `post_cancel` against a live server (idempotent); streaming
  train cancel surfaces partial losses via
  `ClientError::Cancelled` through the client SSE parser.

Contract:

- `contracts/serve-contract/sessions-and-eval.md` -- documents
  `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/cancel` (request/response shape,
  401/404 errors, idempotence), the InterruptMap mechanism
  (why a parallel map rather than reusing the sessions map),
  the "one op" latency floor for in-builtin cancels, and the
  new `event: cancelled` SSE frame schema. The non-goals list
  retires the cancellation item with a pointer to the new
  section.

Quality gates:

- `cargo test -p mlpl-eval --test interrupt_tests` (9), `cargo
  test -p mlpl-serve --test cancel_tests` (5), `cargo test -p
  mlpl-repl --test connect_cancel_tests` (5), `cargo test
  --workspace` -- all green.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
  -- zero warnings.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` -- clean.
- `markdown-checker -f "contracts/serve-contract/sessions-and-eval.md"`
  -- valid.
- `sw-checklist` -- 134 failed (held vs baseline). Refactors
  performed during this commit to keep parity: moved
  `cancel_train` from `eval.rs` into `interrupt.rs` as
  `enrich_train_cancel`; extracted `Environment::emit_metrics`
  to shrink `eval_train` under 50 LOC; extracted
  `handlers::install_session_interrupt` shared between
  `eval_handler` and `eval_stream_handler` to keep both under
  50 LOC; trimmed `EvalError::Cancelled`'s `Display` impl to a
  single-line arm.

Out of scope (later steps in this saga):

- Viz storage endpoint + URL-fetch in connect mode (step 004).
- Non-SVG viz cache + format table (step 005).
- Web REPL connect mode (Phase 4).
- Session persistence (Phase 5).

sw-checklist: 134 (held)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

content.content:
=== PLAN ===
# Multi-client UI Follow-up Milestone (Saga 21.5)

## Why this exists

Saga 21 shipped the MVP CLI server (`mlpl-serve`) and its first
client (`mlpl-repl --connect`). The MVP carved out a deliberately
long list of follow-ups to keep the initial server contract small;
those follow-ups are documented in
`docs/using-cli-server.md#non-goals-deferred`. R1 (v0.18.0) layered
the MLX peer on top and proved the orchestrator/peer shape works.
After two saga cycles of real use, the MVP contract has held -- it
is time to pick up the deferred work.

Saga 21.5 turns the MVP server into the surface other clients
(browser, ratatui, Emacs, desktop GUI) and other workloads (long
training runs, image batches) can actually depend on. The headline
unlock is browser-runs-against-server: today `apps/mlpl-web` runs
entirely in WASM and cannot reach `mlpl-serve` at all, which
forecloses any "browser triggers training on the MLX peer" demo.

This is also the prerequisite for Saga 29 (Vision Transformer
track); the "thorough" ViT demo wants to train on the MLX peer and
have its loss curve stream into the browser REPL. Without 21.5,
that story stays hypothetical.

Goal ranking applied:

- **Utility** leads: every follow-up listed here unblocks a
  user-visible scenario the MVP could not.
- **Correctness**: the contract changes here are additive but
  load-bearing for every future client. Wire format and error
  taxonomy decisions cost more to undo later than now.
- **Educational**: live loss curves and attention-during-training
  visualization are obvious teaching wins for the web tutorial.
- **Performance** is explicitly last; streaming and dtype changes
  are about *what is possible*, not about microseconds.

## Non-goals

- **Multi-tenant isolation / capability scoping.** Sessions are
  still per-server-process; per-client capability tokens (read-only
  vs eval, scoped namespaces) are out.
- **Distributed eval / horizontal sharding.** That story belongs to
  R3.
- **Persistent storage of model weights.** Save / load model
  artifacts is still the Saga 15 follow-up. Sessions persist enough
  to survive a server-restart and rebind clients; the weights
  themselves go nowhere unless `save_model` ships separately.
- **Authentication beyond bearer tokens.** mTLS, SSO, OIDC are all
  follow-ups, gated on a real threat-model write-up.
- **WebSocket transport.** SSE covers streaming for MVP needs; the
  WebSocket variant explicitly carved out by Saga 21 stays out of
  scope here too. Revisit if a use case forces it.
- **Web client architectural rewrite.** Re-route the existing
  `apps/mlpl-web` WASM client to the server *behind a feature flag*;
  do not collapse the WASM-only path. Two modes shipped in parallel
  is fine for one saga -- the WASM mode keeps the offline tutorial
  story alive.

## Quality requirements (every step)

Identical to Saga 23. TDD, all four `cargo` gates +
`markdown-checker` + `sw-checklist` green, `/mw-cp` checkpoint,
push after every commit. Web UI changes rebuild `pages/` via
`scripts/build-pages.sh`. `.agentrail/` committed.

Server changes have an additional requirement: the
`contracts/serve-contract/` prose specs are updated *in the same
commit* as the implementation. The MVP set a precedent that the
contract is authoritative; we honor it.

## What already exists

- `crates/mlpl-serve` REST skeleton: sessions, eval, inspect,
  health, constant-time bearer auth (Saga 21).
- `mlpl-repl --connect <url>` thin client (Saga 21).
- `services/mlpl-mlx-serve` MLX peer with opaque `DeviceTensor`
  handles, strict cross-device CPU faults, `to_device("cpu", x)`
  materialization, f64-only wire (R1).
- `MLPL_CACHE_DIR` CLI viz cache (Saga 21).
- `apps/mlpl-web` WASM REPL with tutorial, demo dropdown,
  numeric-summary accordion (Saga 8 onward).

## Phases

The deferred Saga-21 follow-ups split cleanly along blast radius.
Ship the small, additive ones first; save the surface-changing
ones for the back half.

### Phase 1 -- Server-Sent-Events streaming eval (2 steps)

#### Step 001 -- SSE endpoint scaffold
New `POST /v1/sessions/<id>/eval_stream` that returns
`text/event-stream`. Server emits one `event: ready` on accept,
zero-or-more `event: metric` events for `_metric =` captures inside
the program, then `event: done` with the final value or `event:
error` with the structured error. MVP `/eval` keeps working
verbatim. Tests: SSE round-trip on a 10-step `train { }`, metric
events arrive in order, `done` payload matches the non-streaming
endpoint's response body byte-for-byte. Browser-fetch and
`reqwest::EventStream` both exercised.

#### Step 002 -- live `last_losses` over SSE in the connect client
`mlpl-repl --connect` learns a `--stream` flag (and reads
`MLPL_REPL_STREAM=1`) that routes every eval through the SSE
endpoint. The default is non-streaming so existing scripts stay
quiet. When streaming, `_metric` events redraw the same one-line
loss display the local REPL already uses for `train { }`. Tests:
the same `demos/tiny_lm.mlpl` program produces the same final
value over streaming and non-streaming paths.

### Phase 2 -- Cancellation (1 step)

#### Step 003 -- cancellation endpoint + cooperative interrupt
`POST /v1/sessions/<id>/cancel` flips a session-scoped
`AtomicBool`. The evaluator threads an `Interrupt` token through
`eval_program` and checks it at the head of every loop iteration
(`for`, `train`, `repeat`) plus before every builtin dispatch. On
trip, raises `EvalError::Cancelled` with the current step number
and the partial `last_losses`. `mlpl-repl --connect` binds Ctrl-C
on the second press to a cancel POST. Tests: cancel mid-`train`
returns the partial loss curve, cancel mid-builtin returns
promptly, double-cancel is idempotent.

### Phase 3 -- Visualization storage (2 steps)

#### Step 004 -- viz storage endpoint
`POST /v1/viz` stores an SVG / PNG / HTML / JSON payload and
returns a content-addressed URL (`/v1/viz/<sha256-prefix>`). `GET`
serves the bytes back with the right `Content-Type`. The server's
eval pipeline writes any returned viz value to viz storage *and*
to the local cache dir if `MLPL_CACHE_DIR` is set, returning the
URL in the eval response. `mlpl-repl --connect` prints both `viz:
<url>` and `viz: <local-path>` when both are present.

#### Step 005 -- non-SVG viz cache + format table
The `is_svg_string` detector grows into a small format table:
`<svg`, `<!DOCTYPE html`, magic-byte PNG/JPEG sniffing, and an
explicit `application/json` opt-in for traces. Extends both the
`MLPL_CACHE_DIR` path and the viz storage endpoint. Demo: capture
a `loss_curve(last_losses)` PNG, fetch it back via the URL, render
in a browser tab.

### Phase 4 -- Web UI re-routing (3 steps)

#### Step 006 -- web REPL gains a connect mode behind a feature flag
A new `?connect=<url>` query string (or a settings panel toggle)
switches the web REPL from the in-process WASM evaluator to the
remote one. Same evaluator entry point, two transports. The WASM
path stays the default. Tests: hand-rolled Playwright (or the
existing `mcp__playwright__*` tools) round-trip on `iota(5) + 1`
producing the same display in both modes.

#### Step 007 -- live training in the browser
The web REPL consumes the Phase 1 SSE endpoint when a `train { }`
runs in connect mode. The existing loss-curve UI piece updates in
place (line draws as metrics arrive). The cancel button hooks the
Phase 2 endpoint. Tutorial gains a "Train remotely" lesson.

#### Step 008 -- visualization rendering via storage URL
In connect mode the web REPL fetches viz bytes from the Phase 3
storage endpoint rather than expecting an inline payload. The
`<details>` numeric-summary accordion still renders inline; only
binary viz routes through storage.

### Phase 5 -- Persistence (2 steps)

#### Step 009 -- session re-attach across client restart
`mlpl-repl --connect --session <id> --token <tok>` rebinds to an
existing server-side session instead of creating a new one.
`/v1/sessions/<id>` (GET) returns the session metadata
(creation time, last-eval timestamp, vars / models / tokenizers
summaries). The token persists across REPL restarts via a small
keyring entry (or `MLPL_REPL_SESSION_FILE` env var for non-keyring
hosts).

#### Step 010 -- session persistence across server restart
Server-side: dump the `Environment` for every session to a
single-file SQLite DB on a configurable interval (`--persist
<path>` enables; default off). On startup, restore sessions from
that file. Tests: train a tiny model, restart the server, rebind
the client to the same session ID, `:vars` shows the same workspace
state. Out of scope: cross-machine migration.

### Phase 6 -- Wider wire dtypes (1 step)

#### Step 011 -- f32 + u8 over the MLX peer wire
`services/mlpl-mlx-serve/src/wire.rs` grows two dtype slots beyond
the current f64-only path: `DTYPE_F32 = 1`, `DTYPE_U8 = 2`. The
peer protocol uses the dtype the orchestrator sends; the
orchestrator picks dtype based on the source MLPL array. Image
tensors materialize as u8 at the source and stay u8 over the wire
until the first arithmetic op upgrades them. Tests: round-trip
f32 and u8 fixtures, parity vs f64 on a fixed-seed training step
(within tolerance).

### Phase 7 -- Docs + release (2 steps)

#### Step 012 -- using-cli-server.md retrospective + new client lessons
Move every Phase 1-6 item out of the "Non-goals (deferred)" list
into the main body of `docs/using-cli-server.md`. Add a "Streaming
and cancellation" section and a "Web UI in connect mode" section.
Two new web REPL tutorial lessons: "Connect to a remote MLPL
server" and "Long training, live loss". Update `docs/status.md`
one-liner and `docs/saga.md` Saga 21.5 entry.

#### Step 013 -- release v0.20.0
Bump workspace version. Tag `v0.20.0`. Push commit and tag.
Verify the pages workflow deploys the updated tutorial list and
the web REPL connect-mode toggle.

## Planned steps

| # | Slug | Phase | What it delivers |
|---|------|-------|------------------|
| 001 | sse-endpoint-scaffold        | 1 | `/eval_stream` SSE endpoint, metric/done/error events |
| 002 | sse-connect-client           | 1 | `mlpl-repl --connect --stream` consumes SSE |
| 003 | cancellation                 | 2 | `/cancel` + Interrupt token + Ctrl-Ctrl-C bind |
| 004 | viz-storage-endpoint         | 3 | `POST /v1/viz` + URL fetch, eval pipeline integration |
| 005 | viz-format-table             | 3 | PNG/HTML/JSON detection in cache + storage |
| 006 | web-repl-connect-mode        | 4 | `?connect=<url>` toggle, dual-transport evaluator |
| 007 | web-repl-streaming-train     | 4 | live loss curves over SSE in the browser |
| 008 | web-repl-viz-storage         | 4 | browser fetches viz bytes from the storage endpoint |
| 009 | session-reattach-client      | 5 | `--session <id> --token <tok>` reconnect |
| 010 | session-persist-server       | 5 | SQLite session persistence across restarts |
| 011 | wire-f32-u8                  | 6 | f32 / u8 dtypes on the MLX peer wire |
| 012 | docs-and-tutorials           | 7 | `using-cli-server.md` rewrite, two new lessons |
| 013 | release-v020                 | 7 | version bump, tag, deploy |

Thirteen steps. Phase 1 + 2 + 3 deliver a usable streaming server
on their own; if scope pressure hits, Phase 5 (persistence) is the
easiest to split into a Saga 21.6.

## Success criteria

- A `train 200 { }` block in `mlpl-repl --connect --stream` shows
  the loss decreasing line-by-line in the terminal.
- Ctrl-C twice during a long `train` cancels cleanly and prints
  the partial `last_losses` so far.
- `apps/mlpl-web` with `?connect=http://localhost:6464` runs the
  same `demos/tiny_lm.mlpl` source as the WASM path, produces the
  same final loss, and renders the loss curve as it trains.
- `mlpl-repl --connect --session <id> --token <tok>` re-attaches
  to a session after a client restart and sees the same `:vars`.
- A server restart with `--persist /tmp/sessions.db` brings the
  same `:vars` back.
- An image tensor materialized as u8 on the orchestrator stays
  u8 on the wire to `mlpl-mlx-serve` and is decoded to f32 (or
  promoted to f64) at the peer; the wire-size measurement is a
  recorded `cargo bench` line in `docs/benchmarks.md`.
- The existing offline-tutorial flow on `apps/mlpl-web`
  (WASM-only mode) keeps working with zero regressions.
- All eight items listed under "Non-goals (deferred)" in
  `docs/using-cli-server.md` (except LLM proxy and WebSocket) have
  moved into the main body or into a clearly-named follow-up.

## Risks and open questions

- **CORS for browser-against-server.** `apps/mlpl-web` running on
  `https://sw-ml-study.github.io/sw-mlpl/` cannot hit a localhost
  server without explicit CORS headers. Decide between
  ship-permissive-CORS (easy, slightly worrying) and ship
  `mlpl-serve` with a `--cors-allow <origin>` flag (safer, one
  more knob). Prefer the flag.
- **SSE through HTTP/2 proxies.** Some corporate proxies buffer
  SSE; document the mitigation (`X-Accel-Buffering: no`,
  flush-after-event) rather than chasing every quirk.
- **Cancellation cooperatively.** Pure-arithmetic builtins on
  large arrays don't yield. First version checks at op boundaries
  only; document the latency floor (one op = uncancellable). If
  this bites, add periodic checks inside the array loops as a
  follow-up.
- **SQLite for session persistence.** Workspace state includes
  models, tokenizers, experiments -- all serializable but not yet
  via a stable on-disk format. The simplest implementation
  serializes the in-memory `Environment` via serde + bincode and
  blobs it into one row per session. Schema migration becomes a
  problem at the first incompatible change; a `--persist-version`
  on the file is the cheap mitigation.
- **u8 wire dtype semantics.** On the peer, u8 stays u8 only as
  long as no arithmetic op touches it; the first `add` / `mul`
  promotes to f32 or f64. Specify the promotion ladder explicitly
  in the wire contract so client and peer agree.
- **Web UI dual-mode complexity.** Two transports doubles the
  test surface. Mitigation: a small evaluator-trait abstraction
  in `apps/mlpl-web/src/eval.rs` with two impls (WASM, REST), and
  one shared contract test that both impls satisfy on a fixture
  program.
- **LLM proxy is deferred again.** The proxy that lets browser
  `llm_call` reach a server-side allow-listed Ollama explicitly
  stays out of scope here -- it wants its own security review and
  the threat-model write-up that goes with that. A follow-up
  Saga 21.6 picks it up once the rest of Phase 1-7 has settled.

=== PLAN ===
# Multi-client UI Follow-up Milestone (Saga 21.5)

## Why this exists

Saga 21 shipped the MVP CLI server (`mlpl-serve`) and its first
client (`mlpl-repl --connect`). The MVP carved out a deliberately
long list of follow-ups to keep the initial server contract small;
those follow-ups are documented in
`docs/using-cli-server.md#non-goals-deferred`. R1 (v0.18.0) layered
the MLX peer on top and proved the orchestrator/peer shape works.
After two saga cycles of real use, the MVP contract has held -- it
is time to pick up the deferred work.

Saga 21.5 turns the MVP server into the surface other clients
(browser, ratatui, Emacs, desktop GUI) and other workloads (long
training runs, image batches) can actually depend on. The headline
unlock is browser-runs-against-server: today `apps/mlpl-web` runs
entirely in WASM and cannot reach `mlpl-serve` at all, which
forecloses any "browser triggers training on the MLX peer" demo.

This is also the prerequisite for Saga 29 (Vision Transformer
track); the "thorough" ViT demo wants to train on the MLX peer and
have its loss curve stream into the browser REPL. Without 21.5,
that story stays hypothetical.

Goal ranking applied:

- **Utility** leads: every follow-up listed here unblocks a
  user-visible scenario the MVP could not.
- **Correctness**: the contract changes here are additive but
  load-bearing for every future client. Wire format and error
  taxonomy decisions cost more to undo later than now.
- **Educational**: live loss curves and attention-during-training
  visualization are obvious teaching wins for the web tutorial.
- **Performance** is explicitly last; streaming and dtype changes
  are about *what is possible*, not about microseconds.

## Non-goals

- **Multi-tenant isolation / capability scoping.** Sessions are
  still per-server-process; per-client capability tokens (read-only
  vs eval, scoped namespaces) are out.
- **Distributed eval / horizontal sharding.** That story belongs to
  R3.
- **Persistent storage of model weights.** Save / load model
  artifacts is still the Saga 15 follow-up. Sessions persist enough
  to survive a server-restart and rebind clients; the weights
  themselves go nowhere unless `save_model` ships separately.
- **Authentication beyond bearer tokens.** mTLS, SSO, OIDC are all
  follow-ups, gated on a real threat-model write-up.
- **WebSocket transport.** SSE covers streaming for MVP needs; the
  WebSocket variant explicitly carved out by Saga 21 stays out of
  scope here too. Revisit if a use case forces it.
- **Web client architectural rewrite.** Re-route the existing
  `apps/mlpl-web` WASM client to the server *behind a feature flag*;
  do not collapse the WASM-only path. Two modes shipped in parallel
  is fine for one saga -- the WASM mode keeps the offline tutorial
  story alive.

## Quality requirements (every step)

Identical to Saga 23. TDD, all four `cargo` gates +
`markdown-checker` + `sw-checklist` green, `/mw-cp` checkpoint,
push after every commit. Web UI changes rebuild `pages/` via
`scripts/build-pages.sh`. `.agentrail/` committed.

Server changes have an additional requirement: the
`contracts/serve-contract/` prose specs are updated *in the same
commit* as the implementation. The MVP set a precedent that the
contract is authoritative; we honor it.

## What already exists

- `crates/mlpl-serve` REST skeleton: sessions, eval, inspect,
  health, constant-time bearer auth (Saga 21).
- `mlpl-repl --connect <url>` thin client (Saga 21).
- `services/mlpl-mlx-serve` MLX peer with opaque `DeviceTensor`
  handles, strict cross-device CPU faults, `to_device("cpu", x)`
  materialization, f64-only wire (R1).
- `MLPL_CACHE_DIR` CLI viz cache (Saga 21).
- `apps/mlpl-web` WASM REPL with tutorial, demo dropdown,
  numeric-summary accordion (Saga 8 onward).

## Phases

The deferred Saga-21 follow-ups split cleanly along blast radius.
Ship the small, additive ones first; save the surface-changing
ones for the back half.

### Phase 1 -- Server-Sent-Events streaming eval (2 steps)

#### Step 001 -- SSE endpoint scaffold
New `POST /v1/sessions/<id>/eval_stream` that returns
`text/event-stream`. Server emits one `event: ready` on accept,
zero-or-more `event: metric` events for `_metric =` captures inside
the program, then `event: done` with the final value or `event:
error` with the structured error. MVP `/eval` keeps working
verbatim. Tests: SSE round-trip on a 10-step `train { }`, metric
events arrive in order, `done` payload matches the non-streaming
endpoint's response body byte-for-byte. Browser-fetch and
`reqwest::EventStream` both exercised.

#### Step 002 -- live `last_losses` over SSE in the connect client
`mlpl-repl --connect` learns a `--stream` flag (and reads
`MLPL_REPL_STREAM=1`) that routes every eval through the SSE
endpoint. The default is non-streaming so existing scripts stay
quiet. When streaming, `_metric` events redraw the same one-line
loss display the local REPL already uses for `train { }`. Tests:
the same `demos/tiny_lm.mlpl` program produces the same final
value over streaming and non-streaming paths.

### Phase 2 -- Cancellation (1 step)

#### Step 003 -- cancellation endpoint + cooperative interrupt
`POST /v1/sessions/<id>/cancel` flips a session-scoped
`AtomicBool`. The evaluator threads an `Interrupt` token through
`eval_program` and checks it at the head of every loop iteration
(`for`, `train`, `repeat`) plus before every builtin dispatch. On
trip, raises `EvalError::Cancelled` with the current step number
and the partial `last_losses`. `mlpl-repl --connect` binds Ctrl-C
on the second press to a cancel POST. Tests: cancel mid-`train`
returns the partial loss curve, cancel mid-builtin returns
promptly, double-cancel is idempotent.

### Phase 3 -- Visualization storage (2 steps)

#### Step 004 -- viz storage endpoint
`POST /v1/viz` stores an SVG / PNG / HTML / JSON payload and
returns a content-addressed URL (`/v1/viz/<sha256-prefix>`). `GET`
serves the bytes back with the right `Content-Type`. The server's
eval pipeline writes any returned viz value to viz storage *and*
to the local cache dir if `MLPL_CACHE_DIR` is set, returning the
URL in the eval response. `mlpl-repl --connect` prints both `viz:
<url>` and `viz: <local-path>` when both are present.

#### Step 005 -- non-SVG viz cache + format table
The `is_svg_string` detector grows into a small format table:
`<svg`, `<!DOCTYPE html`, magic-byte PNG/JPEG sniffing, and an
explicit `application/json` opt-in for traces. Extends both the
`MLPL_CACHE_DIR` path and the viz storage endpoint. Demo: capture
a `loss_curve(last_losses)` PNG, fetch it back via the URL, render
in a browser tab.

### Phase 4 -- Web UI re-routing (3 steps)

#### Step 006 -- web REPL gains a connect mode behind a feature flag
A new `?connect=<url>` query string (or a settings panel toggle)
switches the web REPL from the in-process WASM evaluator to the
remote one. Same evaluator entry point, two transports. The WASM
path stays the default. Tests: hand-rolled Playwright (or the
existing `mcp__playwright__*` tools) round-trip on `iota(5) + 1`
producing the same display in both modes.

#### Step 007 -- live training in the browser
The web REPL consumes the Phase 1 SSE endpoint when a `train { }`
runs in connect mode. The existing loss-curve UI piece updates in
place (line draws as metrics arrive). The cancel button hooks the
Phase 2 endpoint. Tutorial gains a "Train remotely" lesson.

#### Step 008 -- visualization rendering via storage URL
In connect mode the web REPL fetches viz bytes from the Phase 3
storage endpoint rather than expecting an inline payload. The
`<details>` numeric-summary accordion still renders inline; only
binary viz routes through storage.

### Phase 5 -- Persistence (2 steps)

#### Step 009 -- session re-attach across client restart
`mlpl-repl --connect --session <id> --token <tok>` rebinds to an
existing server-side session instead of creating a new one.
`/v1/sessions/<id>` (GET) returns the session metadata
(creation time, last-eval timestamp, vars / models / tokenizers
summaries). The token persists across REPL restarts via a small
keyring entry (or `MLPL_REPL_SESSION_FILE` env var for non-keyring
hosts).

#### Step 010 -- session persistence across server restart
Server-side: dump the `Environment` for every session to a
single-file SQLite DB on a configurable interval (`--persist
<path>` enables; default off). On startup, restore sessions from
that file. Tests: train a tiny model, restart the server, rebind
the client to the same session ID, `:vars` shows the same workspace
state. Out of scope: cross-machine migration.

### Phase 6 -- Wider wire dtypes (1 step)

#### Step 011 -- f32 + u8 over the MLX peer wire
`services/mlpl-mlx-serve/src/wire.rs` grows two dtype slots beyond
the current f64-only path: `DTYPE_F32 = 1`, `DTYPE_U8 = 2`. The
peer protocol uses the dtype the orchestrator sends; the
orchestrator picks dtype based on the source MLPL array. Image
tensors materialize as u8 at the source and stay u8 over the wire
until the first arithmetic op upgrades them. Tests: round-trip
f32 and u8 fixtures, parity vs f64 on a fixed-seed training step
(within tolerance).

### Phase 7 -- Docs + release (2 steps)

#### Step 012 -- using-cli-server.md retrospective + new client lessons
Move every Phase 1-6 item out of the "Non-goals (deferred)" list
into the main body of `docs/using-cli-server.md`. Add a "Streaming
and cancellation" section and a "Web UI in connect mode" section.
Two new web REPL tutorial lessons: "Connect to a remote MLPL
server" and "Long training, live loss". Update `docs/status.md`
one-liner and `docs/saga.md` Saga 21.5 entry.

#### Step 013 -- release v0.20.0
Bump workspace version. Tag `v0.20.0`. Push commit and tag.
Verify the pages workflow deploys the updated tutorial list and
the web REPL connect-mode toggle.

## Planned steps

| # | Slug | Phase | What it delivers |
|---|------|-------|------------------|
| 001 | sse-endpoint-scaffold        | 1 | `/eval_stream` SSE endpoint, metric/done/error events |
| 002 | sse-connect-client           | 1 | `mlpl-repl --connect --stream` consumes SSE |
| 003 | cancellation                 | 2 | `/cancel` + Interrupt token + Ctrl-Ctrl-C bind |

| 005 | viz-format-table             | 3 | PNG/HTML/JSON detection in cache + storage |
| 006 | web-repl-connect-mode        | 4 | `?connect=<url>` toggle, dual-transport evaluator |
| 007 | web-repl-streaming-train     | 4 | live loss curves over SSE in the browser |
| 008 | web-repl-viz-storage         | 4 | browser fetches viz bytes from the storage endpoint |
| 009 | session-reattach-client      | 5 | `--session <id> --token <tok>` reconnect |
| 010 | session-persist-server       | 5 | SQLite session persistence across restarts |
| 011 | wire-f32-u8                  | 6 | f32 / u8 dtypes on the MLX peer wire |
| 012 | docs-and-tutorials           | 7 | `using-cli-server.md` rewrite, two new lessons |
| 013 | release-v020                 | 7 | version bump, tag, deploy |

Thirteen steps. Phase 1 + 2 + 3 deliver a usable streaming server
on their own; if scope pressure hits, Phase 5 (persistence) is the
easiest to split into a Saga 21.6.

## Success criteria

- A `train 200 { }` block in `mlpl-repl --connect --stream` shows
  the loss decreasing line-by-line in the terminal.
- Ctrl-C twice during a long `train` cancels cleanly and prints
  the partial `last_losses` so far.
- `apps/mlpl-web` with `?connect=http://localhost:6464` runs the
  same `demos/tiny_lm.mlpl` source as the WASM path, produces the
  same final loss, and renders the loss curve as it trains.
- `mlpl-repl --connect --session <id> --token <tok>` re-attaches
  to a session after a client restart and sees the same `:vars`.
- A server restart with `--persist /tmp/sessions.db` brings the
  same `:vars` back.
- An image tensor materialized as u8 on the orchestrator stays
  u8 on the wire to `mlpl-mlx-serve` and is decoded to f32 (or
  promoted to f64) at the peer; the wire-size measurement is a
  recorded `cargo bench` line in `docs/benchmarks.md`.
- The existing offline-tutorial flow on `apps/mlpl-web`
  (WASM-only mode) keeps working with zero regressions.
- All eight items listed under "Non-goals (deferred)" in
  `docs/using-cli-server.md` (except LLM proxy and WebSocket) have
  moved into the main body or into a clearly-named follow-up.

## Risks and open questions

- **CORS for browser-against-server.** `apps/mlpl-web` running on
  `https://sw-ml-study.github.io/sw-mlpl/` cannot hit a localhost
  server without explicit CORS headers. Decide between
  ship-permissive-CORS (easy, slightly worrying) and ship
  `mlpl-serve` with a `--cors-allow <origin>` flag (safer, one
  more knob). Prefer the flag.
- **SSE through HTTP/2 proxies.** Some corporate proxies buffer
  SSE; document the mitigation (`X-Accel-Buffering: no`,
  flush-after-event) rather than chasing every quirk.
- **Cancellation cooperatively.** Pure-arithmetic builtins on
  large arrays don't yield. First version checks at op boundaries
  only; document the latency floor (one op = uncancellable). If
  this bites, add periodic checks inside the array loops as a
  follow-up.
- **SQLite for session persistence.** Workspace state includes
  models, tokenizers, experiments -- all serializable but not yet
  via a stable on-disk format. The simplest implementation
  serializes the in-memory `Environment` via serde + bincode and
  blobs it into one row per session. Schema migration becomes a
  problem at the first incompatible change; a `--persist-version`
  on the file is the cheap mitigation.
- **u8 wire dtype semantics.** On the peer, u8 stays u8 only as
  long as no arithmetic op touches it; the first `add` / `mul`
  promotes to f32 or f64. Specify the promotion ladder explicitly
  in the wire contract so client and peer agree.
- **Web UI dual-mode complexity.** Two transports doubles the
  test surface. Mitigation: a small evaluator-trait abstraction
  in `apps/mlpl-web/src/eval.rs` with two impls (WASM, REST), and
  one shared contract test that both impls satisfy on a fixture
  program.
- **LLM proxy is deferred again.** The proxy that lets browser
  `llm_call` reach a server-side allow-listed Ollama explicitly
  stays out of scope here -- it wants its own security review and
  the threat-model write-up that goes with that. A follow-up
  Saga 21.6 picks it up once the rest of Phase 1-7 has settled.

[package]
name = "mlpl-serve"
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
version.workspace = true

# Saga 21 step 001: ship as both a binary (so users
# run `mlpl-serve --bind ... --auth ...`) and a
# library (so integration tests + future clients can
# spin up the server in-process via
# `mlpl_serve::server::build_app(...)` /
# `run(...)`).
[lib]
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "mlpl-serve"
path = "src/main.rs"

[dependencies]
mlpl-parser = { path = "../mlpl-parser" }
mlpl-eval = { path = "../mlpl-eval" }
mlpl-array = { path = "../mlpl-array" }
axum = "0.7"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }
# Saga 21.5 step 001: ReceiverStream adapter so an axum SSE
# response can pull events from a tokio mpsc receiver.
tokio-stream = "0.1"
tower = "0.4"
# Saga 25 step A: serve the web UI's static `pages/`
# build alongside the /v1 API so the WASM client and
# the API live on one origin (no CORS plumbing).
tower-http = { version = "0.5", features = ["fs", "trace"] }
# Saga 25 step B: HTTPS support so browsers with
# HTTPS-First Mode (Chrome 147+, Edge, etc.) can reach
# the local UI without disabling browser settings.
# `axum-server` wraps `tokio-rustls`; `rcgen` builds an
# in-memory self-signed cert for `--self-signed`.
axum-server = { version = "0.7", features = ["tls-rustls"] }
rcgen = "0.13"
sha2 = "0.10"
# rustls 0.23 requires an explicit crypto provider; pick
# `ring` (the historical default; aws-lc-rs is the
# alternative and has different licensing).
rustls = { version = "0.23", default-features = false, features = ["ring", "std"] }
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
uuid = { version = "1", features = ["v4", "serde"] }
rand = "0.8"
# Constant-time bearer-token compare; defends against
# timing oracles that could otherwise leak the token
# character-by-character.
subtle = "2"

# Saga R1 step 003: orchestrator forwards
# device("mlx") { ... } blocks to a registered peer
# via blocking reqwest. Async would force tokio into
# the eval crate's call site; blocking keeps the
# evaluator synchronous. The blocking feature
# coexists with the async client used by the
# tokio-based integration tests below.
reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false, features = ["json", "blocking", "rustls-tls", "stream"] }
base64 = "0.22"
bincode = "1"

[dev-dependencies]
# Saga 21: tokio-based api_tests use the async
# reqwest client (still available alongside the
# blocking client enabled in [dependencies] above).

### `POST /v1/viz` and `GET /v1/viz/{id}`

Content-addressed visualization storage. Added in
Saga 21.5 step 004. **Authenticated** when
`auth_mode == Required`: the bearer must match SOME
existing session's token (auth is global, not
session-scoped, so a browser viz fetch in connect
mode does not need to know which session minted the
URL).

`POST /v1/viz`:

```http
POST /v1/viz
Authorization: Bearer <any-valid-session-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"bytes_base64": "PHN2Zy8+", "content_type": "image/svg+xml"}
```

Response (`200 OK`):

```json
{"id": "abcdef0123456789", "url": "/v1/viz/abcdef0123456789"}
```

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
saga 21.5 step 004: /v1/viz storage endpoint + eval-pipeline integration

Adds content-addressed visualization storage to `mlpl-serve`.
`POST /v1/viz` accepts a base64 payload + content_type and
returns `/v1/viz/<sha256-hex-prefix>`; `GET /v1/viz/{id}` serves
the bytes back with the recorded `Content-Type`. The eval
pipeline detects SVG-returning programs (via the existing
`mlpl_cli::viz_cache::is_svg_string` detector) and stashes the
bytes in the store, surfacing a new `viz_url` field on the
`EvalResponse` and on the SSE `done` payload. When the server
has `MLPL_CACHE_DIR` set, the same bytes also land on disk and
the response carries a `viz_local_path` -- the dev-loopback case
(`mlpl-serve` + `mlpl-repl` on one host) lets the REPL open
either the URL or the file directly.

Server implementation:

- `crates/mlpl-serve/src/viz_storage.rs` (new top-level module):
  `VizStore` (`Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, StoredEntry>>>`) +
  `SharedVizStore` alias + `new_store` constructor. Public
  `attach_viz(store, value, kind) -> AttachedViz` shared by
  `eval_handler` and the SSE `spawn_eval_task` so both transports
  surface viz identically. Public `result_to_sse(store, value)`
  builds the terminal SSE frame (`Done` with viz attached, or
  `Cancelled`, or `Error`) so the inline `sse` mod in lib.rs
  stays under its function-count budget. `upload_handler` /
  `get_handler` + shared `require_known_bearer` (which validates
  the bearer against any session's token via the parallel
  `InterruptMap`, so /v1/viz auth does not contend with the
  sessions write lock held by an in-flight eval).
- `crates/mlpl-serve/src/server.rs` -- `AppState` grows a `viz:
  SharedVizStore` field; `build_app_with_peers` routes `POST
  /v1/viz` and `GET /v1/viz/:id`.
- `crates/mlpl-serve/src/handlers.rs` -- `EvalResponse` grows
  `viz_url: Option<String>` and `viz_local_path: Option<String>`
  (both `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`); `eval_handler`
  calls `viz_storage::attach_viz` after eval and threads the
  pair into the response.
- `crates/mlpl-serve/src/lib.rs` sse mod -- `SseEvent::Done`
  grows the same two optional fields; `spawn_eval_task`
  delegates terminal-frame construction to
  `viz_storage::result_to_sse` so the function stays under the
  sw-checklist 50-line LOC budget.
- `crates/mlpl-serve/Cargo.toml` -- depends on `mlpl-cli` for
  the existing `is_svg_string` detector + `write_to_cache`
  helper rather than duplicating them.

Client (`apps/mlpl-repl`):

- `connect.rs` -- `EvalResponse` grows `viz_url` and
  `viz_local_path` (both `Option<String>` with `#[serde(default)]`
  so old payloads continue to deserialize cleanly).
- `connect_stream.rs` -- SSE `done` frame's `DoneData` mirrors
  the new optional fields; `handle_frame` threads them into
  `EvalResponse`.
- `connect_repl.rs` -- `eval_and_print` prints `viz: <url>` and
  `viz: <local-path>` lines (when present) before the formatted
  value. The existing local `viz_cache::transform_value` keeps
  running, so an SVG returned on the same host ALSO produces a
  client-side `viz: <local-path>` line via the user's
  MLPL_CACHE_DIR.

Tests:

- `crates/mlpl-serve/tests/viz_storage_tests.rs` (new, 8 tests):
  POST returns content-addressed URL; idempotent (same bytes ->
  same id); GET returns stored bytes + correct Content-Type;
  GET unknown id is 404; POST/GET 401 without bearer;
  `hist(iota(10), 5)` populates `viz_url` on the eval response
  and the bytes are fetchable via GET; non-SVG eval responses
  leave `viz_url` absent/null.
- `apps/mlpl-repl/tests/connect_viz_tests.rs` (new, 2 tests):
  `connect::eval_remote` surfaces `viz_url` for an SVG-returning
  program; non-SVG responses leave `viz_url` as `None`.

Contract:

- `contracts/serve-contract/sessions-and-eval.md` -- documents
  `POST /v1/viz` and `GET /v1/viz/{id}` (request/response shape,
  401/404 errors, content-addressed idempotence) plus the
  eval-pipeline integration (when the new `viz_url` / `viz_local_path`
  fields appear, what they contain, and how the SSE `done`
  payload mirrors them). The non-goals list retires the
  visualization-storage item.

Quality gates:

- `cargo test -p mlpl-serve --test viz_storage_tests` (8) and
  `cargo test -p mlpl-repl --test connect_viz_tests` (2) and
  `cargo test --workspace` -- all green.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
  -- zero warnings.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` -- clean.
- `markdown-checker -f "contracts/serve-contract/sessions-and-eval.md"`
  -- valid.
- `sw-checklist` -- 135 failed (+1 over baseline 134). The new
  failure is the `mlpl-serve` crate module count ticking from 7
  to 8 (an existing WARN promoted to FAIL). Inline submodule
  (the existing `sse` / `tls` pattern) was tried first but the
  needed surface (5+ functions + the AttachedViz / SseEvent
  helpers + the upload_handler / get_handler pair) pushed
  `lib.rs` over BOTH its 7-fn module-function-count AND its
  500-line file-LOC budgets simultaneously -- a worse outcome
  than the +1 crate module count. The exception trailer below
  flags this.

Out of scope (later steps):

- Non-SVG viz cache + format table (PNG/HTML/JSON magic-byte
  sniffing) (step 005).
- Web REPL connect mode + viz storage URL fetch (Phase 4).

sw-checklist: exception
The +1 in failed-count is the crate module count for
`mlpl-serve` going from 7 to 8 (`viz_storage.rs` added). The
endpoint genuinely needs its own module: the in-memory content-
addressed store, two route handlers, the eval-pipeline attacher,
and the SSE result-to-event builder add ~150 LOC and 5+ fns,
which an inline `pub mod` inside lib.rs cannot absorb without
breaching the existing 7-fn-per-module and 500-LOC-per-file
budgets that already apply to `lib.rs`. Repaying this exception
in a follow-up commit would require either folding viz_storage
back into lib.rs (regressing both file-LOC and fn-count budgets)
or splitting an unrelated module -- neither is a net win.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

- **SQLite for session persistence.** Workspace state includes
  models, tokenizers, experiments -- all serializable but not yet
  via a stable on-disk format. The simplest implementation
  serializes the in-memory `Environment` via serde + bincode and
  blobs it into one row per session. Schema migration becomes a
  problem at the first incompatible change; a `--persist-version`
  on the file is the cheap mitigation.
- **u8 wire dtype semantics.** On the peer, u8 stays u8 only as
  long as no arithmetic op touches it; the first `add` / `mul`
  promotes to f32 or f64. Specify the promotion ladder explicitly
  in the wire contract so client and peer agree.
- **Web UI dual-mode complexity.** Two transports doubles the
  test surface. Mitigation: a small evaluator-trait abstraction
  in `apps/mlpl-web/src/eval.rs` with two impls (WASM, REST), and
  one shared contract test that both impls satisfy on a fixture
  program.

  `llm_call` reach a server-side allow-listed Ollama explicitly
  stays out of scope here -- it wants its own security review and
  the threat-model write-up that goes with that. A follow-up

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
saga 21.5 step 005: VizFormat detection table (SVG/HTML/PNG/JPEG/JSON)

Grows `mlpl_cli`'s viz format detection from "is this SVG?"
into a small lookup table covering five formats:

| Variant     | Detector                              | content_type      | extension |
|-------------|---------------------------------------|-------------------|-----------|
| Svg         | `<svg` (with optional `<?xml ?>` prolog) | image/svg+xml  | svg       |
| Html        | `<!DOCTYPE html` or `<html`           | text/html         | html      |
| Png         | magic bytes `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A` | image/png         | png       |
| Jpeg        | magic bytes `FF D8 FF` (any SOI)      | image/jpeg        | jpg       |
| Json        | explicit `#mlpl-viz: json` opt-in prefix | application/json | json     |

JSON is opt-in because eval routinely produces ordinary string
values that happen to start with `{` -- treating those as viz
would write noise to the cache dir / storage.

Implementation:

- `crates/mlpl-cli/src/viz_format.rs` (new module): `VizFormat`
  enum + `detect(&[u8]) -> Option<VizFormat>` + `content_type`
  + `extension` methods. The detector tries binary magic-bytes
  first (PNG, JPEG), then the explicit JSON opt-in, then UTF-8
  text-prefix sniffing (XML/SVG, HTML).
- `crates/mlpl-cli/src/lib.rs` -- new `pub mod viz_format` plus
  a `pub use VizFormat` at the crate root.
- `crates/mlpl-cli/src/viz_cache.rs` -- `is_svg_string` is now a
  one-line wrapper over `VizFormat::detect == Some(Svg)`. New
  `write_bytes_to_cache(&[u8], &Path) -> io::Result<(PathBuf,
  VizFormat)>` that hashes the bytes, picks the right `.<ext>`
  suffix from the detected format, and writes the file. Returns
  `io::ErrorKind::InvalidData` when no format matches so callers
  can fall back to printing raw / storing opaquely. The original
  `write_to_cache(&str, &Path)` (SVG-only) stays for back-compat.

Module split rationale: keeping `VizFormat` inside `viz_cache.rs`
pushed that module's function count from 5 to 10 (the new enum
adds `detect`, `content_type`, `extension` + the new
`write_bytes_to_cache`), breaching the sw-checklist 7-fn budget.
The split puts the format table in its own module and leaves
`viz_cache.rs` with 6 functions.

Tests:

- `crates/mlpl-cli/tests/viz_format_tests.rs` (new, 14 tests):
  detector returns Svg for SVG payloads (including XML prolog +
  leading whitespace); Html for `<!DOCTYPE html` / `<html`; Png
  for magic bytes (and rejects almost-PNG); Jpeg for `FF D8 FF`;
  Json only when the explicit opt-in prefix is present (plain
  `{...}` returns None); returns None for plain text and empty
  input; content_type and extension lookups match the table
  above; `is_svg_string` still recognizes SVG (back-compat).
- `crates/mlpl-cli/tests/viz_cache_tests.rs` (extended, 5 new):
  `write_bytes_to_cache` lands `.png` / `.html` / `.svg` /
  `.jpg` files for the matching payloads (with bytes round-trip);
  unrecognized bytes return `InvalidData`.
- `crates/mlpl-serve/tests/viz_storage_tests.rs` (extended, 1 new):
  PNG round-trip through `/v1/viz` (POST PNG bytes, GET returns
  `Content-Type: image/png` and the bytes verbatim). The server
  store passes through arbitrary content_types, so no server
  changes were needed beyond the test.

Quality gates:

- `cargo test -p mlpl-cli` (15 + 23 viz_cache + 14 viz_format)
  and `cargo test -p mlpl-serve --test viz_storage_tests` (9)
  and `cargo test --workspace` -- all green.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
  -- zero warnings.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` -- clean.
- `sw-checklist` -- 135 failed (held vs Saga 21.5 step 004's
  baseline; the prior commit's exception lane stands).

Out of scope (later steps): web REPL connect mode (step 006);
web REPL streaming train (step 007); web REPL viz storage fetch
(step 008).

sw-checklist: 135 (held)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git push 2>&1 | tail -3
